title: "L'Estat du Roy de Navarre et de son party en France", BL Harley MS 1582 ff. 263-264 (DECODE R8505)

documents.route: unknown -> unknown (the volume is an English secretary's file; place of writing unknown)

transcription.source: DECODE images IMG_R8505_I39259_P1-P4 at full resolution
transcription.notes: Two passes. The first (ct_p1..p4.txt) was made before the cipher was broken and was 15-30% wrong at sign level. The second, made with the key in hand and checked line by line against the images, covers ff. 263v and 264v (ct2_p3.txt, ct2_p4.txt; 513 and 138 tokens changed). ff. 263r and 264r keep the first pass, corrected only between the shape pairs the second reading proved confusable, every change logged in emendations_all.txt and merges.txt.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of about 50 graphic signs on the 21-letter alphabet, three to six homophones for the frequent letters, plus ten unread nomenclator numbers written between dots.

diacritics.note: no systematic marks seen; dot groups of one to four dots punctuate the runs

system.sibling_key: Navarre's numeric cipher with Segur (BnF 500 Colbert 401, recovered in ../segur) is not this key; it is numeric, not graphic.
system.notes: The letter m is written as a group of two, three or four dots; taking those groups for punctuation is what defeated the first attack. b is a closed oval pierced by a long stem, distinct from the long-s that is u. Nomenclator numbers seen: 6, 21, 26, 36, 51, 57, 72, 81, 99, 721. IC 0.0398 over the first transcription.

prior_solution.where: none found on the DECODE record, in the volume's other records (R8498-R8506), or in print/calendars

conditions.human_role: supplied the DECODE login cookie (stored in the repository) and the target
tools: synthetic control with a known key (control.py)
constrained emendation between proven confusable shapes (emend.py, merge_eq.py)

solution.what: Checked the catalogue's two records: R8501 (Harley 1582 ff. 71-72) proved to be a Stafford 1586 despatch already read in the sibling target harley1582r8500 from its own f.72r decipherment; only R8505 was open.
Fetched the four full-resolution R8505 images with the DECODE session cookie.

Identified the document from its clear text: the French memoir 'L'Estat du Roy de Navarre & de son party en France', written after 1580, on Navarre's standing, places, gentlemen and alliances. DECODE had no title, no date, no author and gave the language as English.
Searched for the memoir in print and in the Calendars of State Papers Foreign 1583-86, and for a graphic-sign Navarre key in DECODE and Tomokiyo's tables.

Transcribed every cipher run on all four sides (3,630 sign tokens, 56 sign names) against a shared sign chart; lines slope by a full line-height across the page, so runs were followed in overlapping band crops.
IC 0.0398 over 3,630 tokens and Sukhotin's vowel test: consistent with a homophonic alphabet of about 50 signs, not with a syllabary (the commonest sign carries 8.7% of the text).
Homophonic annealing with a 1530-1600 French LM (order 4/5, no spaces) and a unigram-frequency penalty, up to 20 restarts x 400k moves, whole text and page by page.

Control experiment: real French enciphered with a 50-sign homophonic key of the same shape, run through the same solver. It failed too, so the solver was the obstacle; a wrong Sukhotin vowel/consonant constraint and a temperature scale far too small for the log-probability deltas. With both fixed the control solves 100%, and 95.5% with 15% of its signs corrupted.
The corrected annealer on the real text produced French immediately; basin hopping and a word-segmentation objective recovered the whole alphabet.
The recovered key had no sign for m or b, impossible for French: the diagnostic that pointed at the transcription rather than the key.

Second, reading-guided transcription of ff. 263v and 264v against the key: the dot groups are m (controls 'et maintenant', 'l'amitie', 'Monsieur de'), phi is b against f = u ('de beau|caire', 'd'une bonne armee'), E3 is s against E = a, T is u against b = n, eq is f. 513 and 138 sign tokens changed.
Read run by run with the clear-text context (reading.txt); 94.6% of deciphered characters fall inside French words.
Content controls: place-names and persons appear where the clear text leads to them - Beaucaire sur le Rosne, Besiers, Carcassonne, Languedoc, Montmorency, d'Espernon, the prince of Parme, Lisbone.
Constrained emendation of the two sides not re-read from the images, between the proven confusable shape pairs only; reading rises to 95.1% measured.

f. 264v (labelled f. 263v until 23 Oct 2026) lines 3.18-3.24 re-read on the image and re-decoded sign by sign with key.json to give one continuous run with its clear context (Italian engineer at Lisbon, whose letters came into the writer's hands; the Lorraine marriage 'pour le rejoindre avec [c]este maison ennemie de la chrestienté e[t] particulierement de l'estat d'Angleterre', 'ceu[s] de Guise en Escosse'); one transcription sign corrected (3.23 b -> T), clear words re-read; key unchanged.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3551 tokens, 57 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.265 per letter; random keys -4.815 (z 7.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.082 (mean -3.101, z 59.1); annealer on the real text -2.352. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): final/f1-f4.txt (the transcription the reading uses) and reading.txt; key key.json / key_letters.txt with the sign chart signs.md

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). reading.txt read line by line: the cipher stretches are word fragments strung together with [#] holes ('E a nouueau T impos du [#81] ou [#] eam ange ries'), some lines almost pure noise; only the clear French around them reads. docs/_check_reading.py: 84 of 185 sentences clean, the clean ones mostly clear text. Relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read, method key recovered from ciphertext-only -> not solved (key work kept as a part); fraction_read 0.951 -> 0.

Re-read brief b28, step 1: DECODE R8505 re-fetched with the cookie (b28_fetch.py): no attachment or comment. DECODE R8010 ('Harley_ms_1582_8') found to be a duplicate record of the same leaves ff. 263r-264v with higher-resolution images; R8009 empty. Web search for the memoir's title: no printed copy.

f. 263r re-read sign by sign on the deskewed R8010 images (b28_deskew.py, b28_line.py): 8 labels corrected (R8505_corrections.tsv, R8505_transcription_f1_b28.txt); the first transcription's 'd' label merged the crossed delta (a) with the crossed epsilon Eb (t) at four places on f. 263r (sentent du, present du, devant Espernon, allie et). Decoder fix: the '#' sign (d) had been read as a code marker by reading.py (b28_r8505_decode.py). Clear French of the five cipher paragraphs of f. 263r transcribed.

Beam decode of all four sides over the documented look-alike signs (b28_r8505_beam.py, fr-1530-despatches 5-gram) and a vs t test for every 'd' token (b28_r8505_alt.py: rectos t 17/22, versos a 35/44); key unchanged. f. 264r improves only in places; spot check of 2.2 on the image confirms the transcription, the run still does not read.

R8505_reading.md (whole memoir, holes marked) and R8505_en.md; alignment b28_r8505_align.py: f. 263r 49/56 decoded words in order in the reading; 9 letters of f. 263r rest on look-alike alternates. Score of the reading body 0.518 (71/137), explicit holes 0.613; f. 263r alone 0.661 / 0.786; before (reading.txt) 0.454. Reader's judgement: f. 263r holds, f. 264r and f. 264v (then labelled 263v) 3.37-3.47 do not. Stays decoded, not read.

Second pass: f. 264r's 25 cipher lines compared with the deskewed R8010 P3 image; 9 label corrections (one-sign f read as II+eq or dot group, T for the open cup, q and d for the crossed epsilon, Pi for Gamma) in R8505_transcription_f2_b28.txt; spot checks of 2.2, 2.5, 2.6 confirm the remaining tokens. f. 264v ll. 3.38-3.46 re-transcribed sign by sign on R8010 P4 (R8505_transcription_f3_b28.txt): the block now decodes in part ('ni selon sa qualite ni selon la leur, les a abandonnees en besoin ... en risee et en proie a leurs ennemis'), so it is not illegible. texts.label: R8505, "L'Estat du Roy de Navarre et de son party en France" (Harley MS 1582 ff. 263-264)
texts.summary: A French political memoir, written after 1580, surveying Henri de Navarre as a political asset for an outside reader: his two 'qualitez' (first prince of the blood, chief of the reformed churches), the places and garrisons he holds in Guyenne, Languedoc, Dauphiné and Provence, his following, his alliances and the marriage question; it belongs with Navarre's embassies to the Protestant powers in the mid-1580s. The cipher carries the sensitive clauses inline in the clear French (d'Espernon, Beaucaire sur le Rosne, Besiers, Carcassonne).

texts.label: L'Estat du Roy de Navarre, fols. 264r-264v, cipher passages, reading by Brice Dudout
texts.summary: A memoir in French on “the state of the King of Navarre and of his party in France”, written in the first person by a man of the Reformed party (“our provinces”, “the letters have come into my hands”) and kept among the papers of an English secretary of state, slips some hundred lines of cipher into its plain text. These are the sensitive passages: the secret organisation of the churches, the reasons for keeping the surety towns, Monsieur’s dealings with the Prince of Parma, and reproaches to “the Queen”, who “has not spent a penny” on them since 1570. Daniel Bourdeau had recovered the alphabet; we re-read the signs on the image and read the text.
